clue.text: Colour of biscuit about to be left out

indicators.note: says the letters for 'about' are removed from the biscuit word

parts.note: a macaroon is an almond biscuit
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone describing a biscuit shade, with a baker leaving something out of the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be left out' removes CA from MACAROON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brownish-crimson shade is a named colour.

clue.text: A clipped English accent

parts.note: clipped hair has been cut

explanation.surface: Describes a crisp, clipped way of speaking English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' here is the written mark over a letter, not a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the acute is the rising diacritic mark placed over vowels such as é.

clue.text: Like company chairman in need of a lifeline?

definitions.text: Like company chairman in need of a lifeline?

parts.words: Like company chairman in need of a lifeline?
parts.note: a chairman sits over the board of directors; split differently the phrase means fallen from a ship into the sea

explanation.surface: Pictures a struggling company boss who needs rescuing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is a chairman's position above the board; as one word it is someone fallen from a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone fallen off a vessel into the water needs a rope thrown to them.

clue.text: End of game inventor set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the name is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: Thomas Edison was the famous American inventor

explanation.surface: An inventor setting up a game finale.
explanation.walkthrough: NO-SIDE is the referee's call ending a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby term: the call that signals the final whistle of a match.

clue.text: The capacity to move in high society? Problem, ultimately, for knight

indicators.note: says one letter stands in place of the knight

parts.note: the nobility are the aristocratic upper class
N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word problem

explanation.surface: Muses on social climbing, then a knight's problem, like a chess puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts M (the last letter of 'Problem') in place of N in NOBILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mobility is the ability to get about freely.

clue.text: Crime in Ireland — young men involved

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled up together

explanation.surface: A news line about youths caught up in an Irish crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: passing dirty cash through legitimate accounts is a financial offence.

clue.text: Shoot after defender gets rebound

indicators.note: the shooting word comes after the defender word

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football
to shoot a gun is to fire it

explanation.surface: A football striker shooting once a defender has had the ball bounce off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a plan that rebounds goes wrong on its maker.

clue.text: Decline drinks, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a cat drinks by lapping, so it laps

explanation.surface: Someone politely declining the offer of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: standards lapse when they decline or slip.

clue.text: Hide in Cuba's capital during coup

indicators.note: puts the letter inside the coup word

parts.note: a coup is a takeover of power

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to go into hiding in Havana during a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hide from danger is to find shelter.

clue.text: Tremendously fast percussion playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with

explanation.surface: A drummer playing at a blistering tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: travelling faster than sound is extremely quick.

clue.text: Fish pasty filled with tail of haddock

indicators.note: the pastry word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a pasty is a kind of pie

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fish pasty stuffed with leftover haddock.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a freshwater predatory species.

clue.text: Annual sporting event in English city, always after first of December

indicators.note: the word for always comes after the month's letter

parts.note: Derby is a city in the English Midlands

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the month

parts.note: AY is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a December sporting fixture in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby Day is the day of the Epsom Derby horse race, held each June.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the date of a famous yearly horse race.

clue.text: Woollen coat to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: slang for to swindle or overcharge

explanation.surface: A woollen garment sent off to be laundered.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sheep's coat and the verb meaning to rip off.

clue.text: A great deal of land in Kansas I auctioned

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A sale of much land in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Understatement: the largest continent is indeed a vast territory.

clue.text: Existing situation in America? Question coming in to us at broadcast

indicators.note: says the two short pieces go inside
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A broadcaster asking questions about the state of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' shuffles TO US AT into STATUO; 'coming in' puts US and Q inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase: the current state of affairs.

clue.text: Is about during a bachelor party, being coarse

indicators.note: places the turned word inside the party word

parts.note: a rave is a wild party

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone being rough and crude at a stag party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IS into SI before 'during' sets it inside the party word; A and B (bachelor) lead the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rough, scratchy surface is harsh to the touch.

clue.text: Underestimate singular redesign of the Rolls

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: redesign suggests rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Underrating a unique remodelling of the Rolls-Royce car.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to undervalue someone or something.

clue.text: Offender in crashed minicar, learner driver

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker involved in a small car crash while learning to drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone guilty of breaking the law is a lawbreaker or wrongdoer.

clue.text: Bureaucrat challenging short chap at the front

indicators.note: the chap word goes at the front

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: daring means bold or challenging

explanation.surface: An official challenging a short man.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a senior civil servant, after the officials of imperial China.

clue.text: Master the choice between pounds and pence once

parts.note: L is the symbol for pounds sterling
a choice between two things is one or the other
D stood for pence in old British money

explanation.surface: A master choosing between pounds and old pence.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pence were written as d.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lord is a master or ruler.

clue.text: Spot leading player dropping old instrument?

parts.note: a zit is a pimple

indicators.note: says that letter is removed

parts.note: the hero is the lead character

explanation.surface: Spotting a lead musician who drops an old instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes O out of HERO, leaving HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flat stringed instrument played on the lap.

clue.text: Mother accepting employment in V&A?

indicators.note: the mother word takes in the other

parts.note: mum is mother
employment means use

explanation.surface: A mother taking a job at the Victoria and Albert in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert, a London gallery of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a famous London institution displaying collections.

clue.text: Court under fire over being correct

indicators.note: in a down clue the court letters go beneath
over means turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: to fire someone is to axe them

explanation.surface: A court finding someone correct when under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AXE into EXA; 'under' puts CT below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: precise and right.

clue.text: Agent, young woman, employed during difficult year

indicators.note: says the young woman is placed inside
difficult hints the letters are awkwardly arranged

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman taking on an agent's job in a tough year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges the letters of 'year' into EARY, which then wraps around the young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an envoy sent on a mission.

clue.text: In the countryside, artist breaking law no end

indicators.note: the artist breaks into the law word
says the final letter is removed

parts.note: a rule is a law
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter flouting a law out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims the final E off the law word to leave RUL; RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pastoral, describing life away from towns.

clue.text: What seaquake projects, at heart?

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Asks what an undersea earthquake sends out.
explanation.walkthrough: An undersea quake throws up water; the central four letters of 'seaquake' give the Latin word for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin word: water, which a seaquake throws up.

clue.text: Bush region portrayed differently in soap

indicators.note: depicted another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A view of the Australian bush shown afresh in a TV drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-running Australian television drama series.

clue.text: March from base, mostly slow going at first

parts.note: the foot is the base of something

indicators.note: most of the word, so drop the last letter

parts.note: the word itself, cut short

indicators.note: at first means at the very start of the word going, so only its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers marching from base, slowly at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long weary trudge on foot.

clue.text: Shake toy

explanation.surface: Shaking a child's plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to jolt noisily, and a baby's toy.
